title: Question 5: Green Economy Bonds ($55 million)

context.text: Placed on the ballot by the General Assembly: the Rhode Island Voter Information Handbook describes Questions 1 through 5 as authorizing the State to borrow through bonds and temporary notes for capital investments under an act passed at the January 2026 session (Chapter 084, Public Laws 2026).

question.text: Shall the act passed by the General Assembly at the January 2026 session, allowing the State of Rhode Island to issue bonds, refunding bonds, and temporary notes to pay for the projects listed below, be approved, and the State be allowed to issue these bonds, refunding bonds, and temporary notes as outlined in the law? 5. GREEN ECONOMY BONDS - $55,000,000 For environmental and recreational purposes, to be allocated as follows: a. Brownfields Remediation and Economic Development - $3,000,000 b. Facility Improvements - $12,000,000 c. Local Recreation Projects - $1,000,000 d. Marine Infrastructure Development - $1,000,000 e. Resilient Rhody Infrastructure Fund - $25,000,000 f. Narragansett Bay Watershed Restoration - $7,000,000 g. Agricultural Land Preservation Commission - $3,000,000 h. Open Space Program - $3,000,000

summary.text: The bond would provide $55,000,000 for environmental and recreational purposes, including brownfield cleanup ($3,000,000), State park, beach and campground facility improvements ($12,000,000), local recreation grants ($1,000,000), marine infrastructure ($1,000,000), the Resilient Rhody Infrastructure Fund ($25,000,000), Narragansett Bay watershed restoration ($7,000,000), the Agricultural Land Preservation Commission ($3,000,000) and the Open Space Program ($3,000,000). Official cost estimate in the handbook (assuming 5% interest and level payments over 20 years): principal $55,000,000, interest $33,267,500, total $88,267,500.

measure.yesMeans: A vote to Approve means that you support the State issuing $55,000,000 in general obligation bonds for environmental and recreational purposes.
measure.noMeans: A vote to Reject means that you are against the State issuing $55,000,000 in general obligation bonds for environmental and recreational purposes.

fiscalImpact.text: Per the Rhode Island Department of State handbook: $55,000,000 in general obligation bonds. Assuming 5% interest and level payments over 20 years, interest is $33,267,500 and total cost $88,267,500 (cost of issuance estimated at 0.4% of principal). Most projects are to be completed within five years of starting; most have a useful life of 25 to 50 years, and conserved open space or farmland is permanent.

supporters.text: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (Director Terry Gray), which promotes the bond on its website and spoke at the Sept. 28 Question 5 campaign kickoff.
Rep. Megan Cotter (D-Exeter) and Sen. Louis DiPalma (D-Middletown), who worked to increase the bond’s resilience funding, per ecoRI News.

researchNotes: The ballot text, approve/reject statements and cost estimates are from the Rhode Island Department of State's 2026 Voter Information Handbook (PDF text extracted and checked by script). The handbook publishes no arguments for or against, and no verbatim argument against the measure was found; the argument lists are left empty so both sides stay balanced (supporters, where found, are listed under supporters). The Secretary of State's website and Ballotpedia blocked automated requests; the five-question list is from the handbook, which covers all statewide referenda. Added (Oct. 19): full text is Article 5 of H 7127 Sub A as amended (enacted as Public Laws 2026 ch. 84); cost figures restate the handbook. No campaign-finance totals were found (the state campaign-finance portal was not queried). The Sept. 28 campaign kickoff is described by ecoRI News (Oct. 5, 2026). No opposing statement was found.
